title: Automated per-customer batching & caching policy engine with safe apply/rollback and tier segmentation
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Goal: Build an automated recommendation and enforcement pipeline that selects per-customer and per-route batching/caching configurations, applies them safely to production, and rolls back automatically when SLO regressions or correctness issues are detected.

Scope:
- Recommendation engine that suggests batch_size, batching_window_ms, prefix_cache_enabled, kv_cache_policy, and quantization hints per customer and per-route based on historical traffic profiles and cost-per-token.
- Policy layer for segmentation (customer tiers: enterprise/standard/free), allowlists/denylists per-route, and manual overrides.
- Safe apply mechanism: dry-run/canary apply, gradual ramping, realtime observability and automatic rollback on SLO or quality regressions.
- Console and API surface to review suggested changes, approve plans, and audit applied changes.
- Runtime agent integrations to accept policy deltas and apply without service restarts.

Non-goals: fully automated model-level quantization changes (out of scope for initial rollout).

Design summary:
1) Offline scorer: nightly job scores each (customer, route) pair on latency-cost-quality Pareto frontier. Produces ranked candidate config deltas with expected savings and risk score.
2) Policy engine & store: stores segmentation rules, allow/deny lists, tier mappings, and safe constraints (min_throughput, slo_latency_p95_guardrail). Evaluates whether a candidate is eligible for automated apply.
3) Apply controller: supports modes (dry-run, canary-percent, phased-apply). Executes controlled config rollouts to runtime agents, monitors fidelity and SLOs via a ruleset, and triggers rollback if anomalous.
4) Observability & auditing: per-change dashboard showing cost delta, latency P50/P95, error rates, and a linked prompt-eval sample to track quality regressions. All changes are logged for compliance and replay.

Success metrics:
- 8-12% average host-level cost reduction on eligible routes in first 30 days after rollout.
- No more than 0.5% of canaries trigger automatic rollback due to correctness issues.
- Time-to-apply (dry-run -> full) under 48 hours for approved changes.

Constraints & safety:
- Never reduce batching below min_batch_size or increase window_ms beyond route_max_latency derived from SLO.
- Allow enterprise-tier customers to opt-out by policy.
- All automated changes require at least one successful dry-run and pass the canary window before full application.

Deliverables:
- Recommendation service (Python) + nightly scorer job.
- Policy store schema additions and enforcement API.
- Apply controller (Kubernetes Job + controller) with canary orchestration.
- Console review flow and API endpoints for approvals.
- E2E tests + dogfood on dedicated cluster for 2 pilot customers.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation engine generates candidate configs for >=90% of routes with historical traffic >100 req/day
Policy engine enforces segmentation, allowlists, and denies according to project config and exposes REST API for updates
Apply controller supports dry-run, canary (1%, 10%), and phased apply to 100% with automatic rollback on SLO degradation
Console exposes suggested changes with diff view, estimated cost delta, and one-click approve/reject
Audit logs capture author, timestamp, dry-run output, canary metrics, and final decision for every automated change
